investigating whether I will be able to use bacula for our backups
salutation
First of all a few typos I found in the user manual (not the beta one):

should that be backslash or /?

There, I hope you can see this as a contribution and not as silly nitpicking.

The manual is very clear and it is very well written. It looks very professional.

Now on to my questions:

Our tape streamer 'expired'. We decided that we don't want to use tapes anymore (this happens once every three years, more or less, and every time all those expensive tapes are sitting there, suddenly worthless). So now we decided we wanted a system that backs up to removable hard disk drives and DVD+/-R. At first look it seems like Bacula would be up to the challenge. We would want to use two fixed drives (daily, weekly), three removable USB2-drives (weekly, for off site storage) and DVD for being able to go back in time indefinitely.

Would such a set up be feasible with Bacula?

I suppose the three removable USB-drives would go into one pool and bacula would be able to tell me which one to bring along and connect. Would it tell me that at the moment it wants to start the backup somewhere in the middle of the night? Or is it possible to have it mail me what it needs during the week or day preceding that backup?

As far as the DVD is concerned, it can always have a blank DVD loaded, so that is not an issue and the two fixed hard drives are also available by definition.

The backup server will run Linux and work with a MySQL database. The systems needing the backup are two NT4-servers. The fixed disks are also sitting in the NT4-servers and I would like to keep them there. Would that be possible? I read that the File Daemon can run on Windows, but I'm not sure about the storage daemon. If the storage daemon cannot run on Windows, is it possible to write it on to a smbfs mount point? Or is it better I just continue xcopying for the daily backup?

Many thanks if you can answer my questions and otherwise too for making such a great product and making it available under the GPL.

Now I'll go and continue reading your manual,

Re: Overriding delegated methods
quotation
Sure. Basically, I have one class that wraps an external process (and provides
other goodies). It has a #puts method to send input to that process, and
receive back parsed output. #puts is called both on its own from external code,
and from within other methods of the same class. The problem then was that the
external process ate more and more memory over time (and no, this optimization
is not premature. Its a definite problem). The solution that came to my mind
was to create a delegating class that counts how many times #puts has been
called, and restarts the process by killing the old wrapper object and creating
a new one (in my app, the calls to #puts were independent of each other, so I
could get away with this). So I overrode #puts, but the calls to #puts in the
original class are not using it. I could put killing/restarting code into the
original class, but I think separating it would be a nicer solution.

quotation
At regular intervals (every X calls to #puts, as above). In one specific
instance, that amounted to around every half hour over a 12 hour period.

quotation
I want all calls to #puts, whether from the delagating or delegated class, to
go through my overridden version (but still have the original accessible via
super() or something).

Re: Eliminating False Spam Score
quotation
Your email gets PRIORITY_NOMAIL score because SpamAssassin 2.x allows
X-Priority headers only with X-Mailer header. SquirrelMail 1.4.0 and later
uses User-Agent header instead of X-Mailer. Since SquirrelMail 1.4.4
you want to use workarounds in SquirrelMail - revert code change in
class/deliver/Deliver.class.php. You can see SquirrelMail code changes in
cvs.sf.net URL.

SquirrelMail does not have to fix anything. Broken part is in SpamAssassin
code and not in SquirrelMail.

Please keep same reply style, don't top post and don't strip relevant
parts of your message. It is hard to follow conversation when you post
your reply on top and remove original email text.
